verifiedAdds.name: Mala Luka cove + Vela Luka sunset beach (Stanići, Omiš riviera)
verifiedAdds.complementsDay: D1 Omiš → Krvavica coast drive (and D1/D2 Makarska base evenings)
verifiedAdds.whyBest: This is the dual-purpose find your D1 is missing: a west-facing cove with what locals repeatedly call THE best sunset in Croatia, AND a genuine self-swim/snorkel cove off the tourist track — directly on the coastal road between the Cetina/Omiš activities and Camping Krvavica, so zero net detour on the drive south. The existing Stanići pin is only the apartment cluster; the cove and its sunset are net-new. Vela Luka is the long west-facing main pebble beach (sun lingers past 20:30, lighting up cliffs and water); Mala Luka, 'just around the corner,' is the smaller locals' cove with clear water for snorkelling. Beats the in-town Makarska sunset because it's quieter, free, and you can swim right up to golden hour. Taste-fit: nature + self-swim + sunset, non-generic, locals' spot.
verifiedAdds.communityNotes: visitomis.hr (official riviera guide) and multiple Croatian beach guides: 'The main beach in Stanići — Velika luka — has the most beautiful sunsets in Croatia. The sun shines over Stanići beach until late in the evening.' 'Just around the corner there is Mala luka, a beautiful cove that's very popular among locals.' A local Omiš-riviera blog (greystonezvecanje) lists Stanići/Mala Luka among the 'more secluded' beaches: 'crystal-clear water and a more peaceful atmosphere... popular with the locals — always a good sign.' Putovnica.net beach DB rates Vela Luka a 600m gravel beach with café/shower/natural shade. The west orientation (sun setting over the open sea, not behind an island) is what makes the sunset claim stand out vs Punta Rata.
verifiedAdds.verifyEvidence:
EXISTS + COORDS VERIFIED: Claimed coords 43.4187/16.7175 resolve to OSM "Mala Luka, Stanići, Grad Omiš" (hamlet at 43.41873/16.71749) within ~10m. Multiple independent sources (putovnica.net, omisinfo.com, beachrex, sandee, croatiahiddengems) confirm Mala Luka is a real, lesser-known cove in Stanići between Nemira and Stanići village.

DESCRIPTION HOLDS (with a naming fix): Sources consistently describe Mala Luka as a SOUTHWEST-facing bay (not strictly "west") divided into two parts — main pebble beach + smaller side coves — that has "the most beautiful sunsets on the Omiš riviera," sun setting in the sea between islands Šolta and Drvenik, AND clear turquoise water with rock formations that are "wonderful places for snorkeling." WORTHWHILE: Strong taste-fit (nature + self-swim/snorkel + sunset, off the main tourist track, on the coastal road south toward Camping Krvavica = ~zero net detour). Caveat for rating: evidence is mostly beach-catalog/local-blog sources rather than Reddit/forum traveler threads, so community-strength is moderate (~3/5), not "repeatedly praised across independent traveler reports." Afternoon W winds can pick up; busy in peak season but eastern coves stay quiet.

verifiedAdds.name: Kupalište na Bunici (Bunica local sunset-swim, Buna/Hodbina)
verifiedAdds.complementsDay: D4 Kravica/Počitelj corridor → D5 Mostar/Blagaj approach
verifiedAdds.whyBest: A LOCALS' river-swim ritual on the Bunica — a different river from every Buna pin you already have, fed by the deepest karst spring in Europe (Vrelo Bunice, 69m), so the water is icy-clear and bath-calm. The cultural draw is exactly the group's vibe: Mostarci come here to 'swim, fish, grill meat and drink beer while watching the sunset' at the abandoned grand 1970s recreation center (once 5,000 bathers/day), now informally reclaimed each summer — zero tour buses, free, self-organised. A genuine off-the-radar swim+sunset combo on the Kravica→Mostar drive, not a guidebook stop. A 16th-c. 13-arch Ottoman bridge (Danijel-pasha) sits nearby at the Buna–Neretva confluence.
verifiedAdds.communityNotes: hercegovina.info: 'kupalište na Bunici i danas privlači mnoge koji žele pobjeći od vrućine' — abandoned after the war but 'citizens informally restore and use the bathing area' every summer, ~15km S of Mostar. klix/Bunica coverage: locals 'swim, fish, roast meat and drink beer while watching the sunset' where the Bunica meets the Buna at Hodbina. Wiki/local sources: endemic softmouth trout, water 'calm flow and pleasant temperature' that taught generations of Mostar kids to swim; Vrelo Bunice spring itself (43.2215/17.8899) is a protected geomorphological monument but DEEP and dangerous to enter — swim at the downstream beach, not the spring eye.

COORDS: Wikipedia places the Buna-Bunica confluence at 43.2445N/17.8516E; the claimed 43.2438/17.8529 sits ~140m SE of the confluence, on the Bunica river just upstream of the mouth — exactly where the recreation/beach zone is. verifiedAdds.name: Vrelo Paljanske Miljacke (Miljacka source + travertine waterfalls, Gornje Pale)
verifiedAdds.whyBest: The Pale-side nature/swim spot the brief wanted, and it sits literally ~200m from the group's D6 'Home in Pale' bed - so it's a zero-drive morning before the D7 Tara departure or an evening wind-down. It's the source of the Miljacka: spring water bubbling up beneath the medieval Gradina/Pavlović fortress ruins, then sliding down a staircase of moss-covered travertine waterfalls ~100-250m downstream. Marked forest trails run from here to the Goli Koran picnic area. A genuine non-touristy local spot (RS side, almost no foreign visitors), with a trout-pond restaurant if they want a quick fish lunch. Pairs with a scramble up to the Gradina ruins for a Pale-valley viewpoint.
verifiedAdds.communityNotes: Local Pale blog palelive.com ('Vodopadi naše mladosti' / 'Waterfalls of our youth'): a beloved childhood-school-trip spot; 'only the bravest boys dared swim there, and only during the hottest August days, because the water at the source was very, very cold' - groups picnic, grill, and chill watermelon and beer in the spring water. klix.ba: 'magnificent nature that leaves you breathless, just two km from Pale.' furaj.ba/toopale: water is a constant ~6-6.5°C; waterfalls are strongest in spring/autumn, thinner in mid-summer - so in June expect a cold karst dip + a waterfall stroll + picnic rather than a warm swim. Forest shade, free, open access; short unpaved spur off the main road by Restoran Vrelo Miljacke.

EXISTS & AS DESCRIBED — corroborated across Wikipedia, Destination Sarajevo, jahorinatravel.com, toopale.com (official Pale tourism org), 033.ba, palelive.com, furaj.ba. On access: 'Do nje možete doći s mora ili se spustiti niz stijene držeći se za uže. Ovdje je prilično strmo pa ovo mjesto ne preporučujemo obiteljima s djecom ili ljudima koji se boje penjanja' — i.e. reach it from the sea or climb down the rocks holding a rope; quite steep, not for families or anyone afraid of climbing. journal.hr/Nomago: 'isolated location and crystal-clear turquoise sea... surrounded by steep cliffs, providing a sense of privacy and peace.' Listed FKK on Google Maps though not officially nudist.

verifiedAdds.name: Bunski kanali — where Buna meets Neretva (two parallel coloured rivers + travertine cascades)
verifiedAdds.complementsDay: D4/D5 Mostar–Blagaj–Počitelj corridor (on the M-17 between Buna and Počitelj)
verifiedAdds.whyBest: A genuinely rare natural phenomenon right on the M-17, ~12-15min south of Mostar with zero net driving: the green Neretva and the blue Buna run side-by-side in parallel channels over a limestone (travertine) barrier before merging, with a series of small Buna cascades. Adds a non-generic, free, uncrowded nature/photo + short-walk stop to a day otherwise full of the heavily-visited Stari Most/Blagaj Tekija circuit — it complements the group's taste (wild karst water, not an old town) and sits between the existing Blagaj/Buna swims and the Počitelj/Kravica block. More a scenic walk + photo phenomenon than a deep swim/jump (honest: TripAdvisor reviewers note no organised swimming and patchy signage).
verifiedAdds.communityNotes: Local portals call it 'mjesto gdje Buna ljubi Neretvu' (the place where Buna kisses Neretva) and 'rijetko viđeni fenomen' — from the bridge you see two distinct water colours flowing alongside each other before merging. TripAdvisor visitors: 'stunning natural phenomenon', 'scary and beautiful at the same time', 'beautiful view from the bridge', and note it's uncrowded and sits 'just meters from the main Mostar–Čapljina highway' with side-road parking by the bridge. Caveats from reviews: poor signage (hard to find), water can look murky, and locals say the whole area floods/submerges in winter — a summer-only spot. Wear proper footwear for the channel terrain.
verifiedAdds.verifyEvidence:
EXISTS — confirmed by multiple independent sources. The Buna doesn't flow straight into the Neretva: the two run side by side for ~850m, with part of the Buna spilling over a travertine barrier creating a line of small waterfalls (up to ~2m, seasonal) before merging — a karst hydrological phenomenon protected as a natural monument since 1970 (HR/EN Wikipedia "Buna Canals", visitbih, SeeSrpska). Located ~10-12km south of Mostar directly on the M-17 Mostar-Čapljina road.

COORDS VERIFIED — EN Wikipedia gives 43°14′25″N 17°50′00″E = 43.2403, 17.8333, ~25m from the claimed 43.2405,17.8335 (well within 300m). This is the canal/bridge spot on the M-17, NOT the Blagaj/Bunica area (one tour-operator page loosely conflates the two, but the authoritative coords + the confluence description place it here). TripAdvisor reviewers confirm a viewing bridge with a side-road parking spot right off the highway.

NET-NEW — nearest existing pins: ba-buna-brzatak-swim (43.2474,17.8402) ~0.94km NE (a separate developed Buna bathing beach, not the confluence); ba-villa-gana-buna (43.232,17.831, accommodation) ~0.94km; ba-zitomislici-monastery (43.208,17.793) ~3.6km S. All outside 500m; this is a distinct phenomenon.

WORTHWHILE (with honest caveats) — fits the group's taste (wild karst water, not an old town); free, uncrowded, zero net driving on the M-17 between the existing Blagaj/Buna swims and the Počitelj/Kravica block. Caveats from reviewers: it's a scenic walk + photo stop rather than a swim/jump site (no reviews mention swimming at the confluence itself), signage is poor ("took a while to find it, but it was worth it"), and one recent reviewer found the water dirty; locals say it can go fully underwater in winter (not a June concern). Best in summer when colours/travertine pop.

verifiedAdds.name: Gornji Stoliv — abandoned stone village + church terrace viewpoint (hike up from Donji Stoliv)
verifiedAdds.complementsDay: D11 Kotor Bay (Camping Mimoza, Donji Stoliv base)
verifiedAdds.whyBest: A self-contained sunset/viewpoint hike that LITERALLY starts at the D11 camp — zero driving. The committed D11 is a packed Kotor-city day (San Giovanni fortress, BBQ Tanjga, old-town bars); this adds a quiet nature+activity option the group actually likes (hidden, abandoned village, ridge view) instead of more old-town. ~45-min shaded chestnut-forest climb on a 150-yr-old stepped path straight up from Donji Stoliv to a church terrace with a full panorama of Perast + Our Lady of the Rocks/Sveti Đorđe islands + the whole bay. Far better golden-hour spot than the city fortress crowd, and it's the trailhead for the longer Vrmac/Sveti Ilija (765m) ridge if they want more.
verifiedAdds.communityNotes: Local blogs are unanimous it's a time-stopped gem: Jasnina Putovanja — '~40 min up from Donji Stoliv on a stepped path donated by a sailor 150+ years ago, still in excellent condition; only 3 permanent residents left, an informal kafana operates, mostly foreign visitors, minimal crowds.' Boka News — 'orderly rocky path through a chestnut forest... unique view of Perast and the islands; St Ilija festival 20 July.' English guides confirm: 'very easy though uphill, ~45 min through shaded chestnut woods, gorgeous panorama of Perast with Our Lady of the Rocks and St George — if short on time in Kotor Bay this is THE place to hike for the views; careful after rain, very slippery.' Down to ~1 inhabited house (1979 earthquake + emigration); church of St Anne has the panoramic platform, plus abandoned olive mills/bakeries.
verifiedAdds.verifyEvidence: EXISTS + as described: Gornji Stoliv is a well-documented abandoned 14th-c. stone village on the northern Vrmac slope (~240-260m) above Donji Stoliv on Kotor Bay, reachable only on foot. Multiple independent sources confirm a ~40-45 min stepped-stone donkey-track climb through chestnut forest, starting by the Church of St Ilija at the shore road (red/white blaze). The panoramic flagged terrace with "the single best view over Perast in the whole Boka" — both islands (Our Lady of the Rocks + Sveti Đorđe/St George) plus the bay's mountain horseshoe — is at the Baroque Church of St ANNE (Sveta Ana), not St Ilija (the claim slightly conflates the two churches; St Ilija is also the 785m Vrmac peak). It is also the trailhead for the longer Vrmac/Sveti Ilija ridge. COORDS: OSM Nominatim resolves Gornji Stoliv to 42.4661878/18.7150364 = claimed 42.4662/18.715 (~5m off; spot-on). NET-NEW: nearest pin is me-camping-mimoza-stoliv (the D11 base) 888m DOWNHILL on the shore — a campsite, not this uphill hike destination; next nearest are the Prčanj/Stoliv WOW villa 2.1km, Perast 2.6km, Fort Goražda 8.8km. Nothing within 500m. WORTHWHILE: hidden abandoned village + golden-hour ridge panorama, light shaded hike starting at the D11 camp (zero driving) — exactly the nature/activity/non-old-town option this group prefers; good one-per-day slack/highlight. NOTE for pin author: label the viewpoint as the Church of St Anne (Sveta Ana) terrace.

verifiedAdds.name: Uvala Trsteno — quiet turquoise fine-sand cove (Budva riviera)
verifiedAdds.complementsDay: D11 Budva → Sveti Stefan → Kotor (morning, before the bay)
verifiedAdds.whyBest: The only swim pin in this Budva stretch is Ploče (the concrete party beach, most expensive + most crowded on the riviera). Trsteno is the opposite and directly on-route ~1.3km north: a tucked-in cove with fine sand, clear azure water and a sandy bottom — locals' choice for a calm clear-water swim with far fewer people. Fits the group's taste (self-swim, hidden-ish cove, non-generic, no party scene) as a morning dip before driving N to the Kotor bay, and it's a no-cost beach (sunbed ~€10 only if wanted).
verifiedAdds.communityNotes: RTV Budva — 'Uvala Trsteno: turquoise sea and fine sand.' Local beach guides: 'known for untouched nature and crystal-clear water; 200m of fine sand, azure sea, sandy seabed; because it's tucked in there's not much room for sunbeds so it's LESS crowded than other beaches; entry free, sunbed ~€10, a few cafés for light bites.' Contrasted explicitly with Ploče which locals call 'the main party beach, packed in season, hardest place to park, priciest on the riviera, foam parties/festivals.'
verifiedAdds.verifyEvidence: EXISTS + well documented. Trsteno is a real ~200m fine-sand cove on the Budva riviera, deeply set into the land (protected from waves/winds), with clear azure water and a shallow sandy bottom. COORDS VERIFIED within ~25m: two independent sources give 42.281618/18.785028 (worldbeachguide/virtlo) and a Sandee map pin at 42.281853/18.784823 — both essentially identical to the claimed 42.2816/18.7848. (I nudged lng from 18.7848 to 18.785 to match the consensus pin; difference is ~17m, immaterial.) NET-NEW: nearest existing pin is me-ploce-beach (42.26992/18.78486) ~1.3km SOUTH — confirmed by my own lat-delta calc (0.01168° ≈ 1.30 km) and corroborated by sources ("Ploce is 0.9 mi from Trsteno"). No other pin within 500m (Jaz ~1.5km E, Mogren further E). WORTHWHILE: TripAdvisor reviewers explicitly prefer Trsteno over busier Mogren for a more relaxed atmosphere and clean/clear water; soft sand "soft as carpet"; free access with optional paid sunbeds (~€5-30). Fits the group: free self-swim cove, non-generic, no club scene — the calm-water opposite of the Ploče party beach. HONEST CAVEATS: (1) not an obscure secret — it's an organized beach that does get crowded in peak season (June=high season) and has a beach-bar with occasional loud turbo-folk music; (2) geographically it sits ~5km WEST of Budva, reached via a short side road off the Adriatic highway near the Jaz cove — so it's a brief detour off the coastal road rather than literally on the through-route, though still very close (~1.3km from the Ploče pin).
